title: Step 1 · Before Umrah
text: step 1 of 8 before umrah 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 01 before umrah let’s get your papers, your body and your heart ready. where am i? at home, before you travel what do i do now? open the “before you go” planner we’ll count down together from 8 weeks to the day you travel, go through nusuk step by step, and look at health tips for the heat. flying from pakistan? here’s what you need: polio and meningitis vaccines, the new nadra vaccine card, ihram on the flight and consulate contacts. tick each one as you go. your ticks stay saved on this phone, so come back anytime. papers visa. umrah is allowed on an umrah visa or a saudi visit/tourist visa. umrah permit in the nusuk app. first, book your umrah time slot in the official nusuk app. please note: you can’t enter for umrah before your permit time. passport valid for at least 6 months from your travel date. just to be sure, confirm with your airline or agent. meningitis vaccine (all pilgrims). acyw or acywx conjugate vaccine within the last 5 years (or polysaccharide within 3 years), at least 10 days before arrival. only if it applies to you: polio or yellow fever vaccines for arrivals from listed countries (pakistan and afghanistan are on the polio list). covid-19 proof for people over 65, pregnant women and those with chronic illness. save your hotel address and group leader’s number on your phone and on paper, just in case. checked september 2026 · health: saudi ministry of health, umrah health requirements 1447h (2026) · permits and visas: ministry of hajj and umrah faq · passport: travel industry guidance. rules can change each season; check again before booking. bookings (nusuk and travel) create your nusuk account (official app of the ministry of hajj and umrah). you’ll use it for all your permits and umrah bookings. umrah visa: hotel booked through nusuk masar. since the 1447h season, a confirmed booking in a licensed hotel, recorded in nusuk masar, is required before an umrah visa is issued. your agent or nusuk does this for you. book your umrah permit for your chosen date and time in the nusuk app (see papers above). train (optional): the haramain high speed railway links jeddah airport (king abdulaziz international), jeddah, makkah and madinah. makkah to madinah takes about 2 hours, a comfortable ride. please book only through the official saudi arabia railways (sar) channels. visiting madinah? book a rawdah (riyad al-jannah) permit in the nusuk app. it is free. men and women have separate times and gates, and you can only enter in your booked slot, so plan your day around it. checked september 2026 · nusuk masar hotel rule: ministry of hajj and umrah (reported by saudi gazette, june 2025) · train: saudi arabia railways / visit saudi · rawdah: nusuk app rules as reported september 2026. booking rules change often; check in the nusuk app before you travel. pack men: 2 plain white ihram sheets, a belt, open sandals. women: loose, modest clothes that cover the body. any colour. unscented soap, shampoo and deodorant, so you stay fresh in ihram. your medicines in original packs, with prescriptions. small bag, water bottle, power bank, a bag for your shoes. heart & mind learn the 4 essential acts: ihram, tawaf, sa‘i, hair. i’ll walk you through each one. practise the talbiyah until it feels natural (see step 2). renew your intention and repent. settle your debts, and ask forgiveness from anyone you may have wronged. what do i say? leaving your home بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ، لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ bismillāh, tawakkaltu ‘ala-llāh, lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh. meaning: in the name of allah. i put my trust in allah. there is no might nor power except with allah. sunan abi dawud 5095 (sahih) setting off on the journey (full travel dua) اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ. سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ، وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَذَا الْبِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَى، وَمِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَى. اللَّهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهُ. اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ، وَالْخَلِيفَةُ فِي الْأَهْلِ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ، وَكَآبَةِ الْمَنْظَرِ، وَسُوءِ الْمُنْقَلَبِ فِي الْمَالِ وَالْأَهْلِ allāhu akbar (×3). subḥāna-lladhī sakhkhara lanā hādhā wa mā kunnā lahū muqrinīn, wa innā ilā rabbinā la-munqalibūn. allāhumma innā nas’aluka fī safarinā hādha-l-birra wa-t-taqwā, wa mina-l-‘amali mā tarḍā. allāhumma hawwin ‘alaynā safaranā hādhā wa-ṭwi ‘annā bu‘dah. allāhumma anta-ṣ-ṣāḥibu fi-s-safar, wa-l-khalīfatu fi-l-ahl. allāhumma innī a‘ūdhu bika min wa‘thā’i-s-safar, wa ka’ābati-l-manẓar, wa sū’i-l-munqalabi fi-l-māli wa-l-ahl. meaning: allah is the greatest (three times). glory be to the one who has placed this at our service; we could not have done it ourselves, and to our lord we will surely return. o allah, we ask you on this journey for goodness and piety, and for deeds that please you. o allah, make this journey easy for us and shorten its distance. o allah, you are the companion on the journey and the one who looks after the family. o allah, i seek refuge in you from the hardship of travel, from distressing sights, and from an evil return to wealth and family. sahih muslim 1342 remember men: practise wearing ihram at home try tying the sheets and belt once before you travel. it makes the real day much easier. expect a lot of walking sa‘i alone is about 3 km. break in comfortable sandals before you go, and your feet will thank you. avoid leaving all the learning until you arrive. you will be tired then, so start now, a little at a time. packing only scented toiletries. you can’t use them once you are in ihram. map next · step 2 enter ihram

title: Step 2 · Ihram
text: step 2 of 8 ihram 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 02 · essential ihram الإحرام ihram is the sacred state of umrah. you enter it with an intention and the talbiyah . remember, the clothes alone are not ihram. where am i? before you pass the meeqat the meeqat is a boundary you must not cross without ihram. don’t worry about missing it: on a plane, the crew usually announces it, and your group leader will tell you which one you pass. the five meeqat dhul-hulayfah (abyar ‘ali) coming from madinah al-juhfah (rabigh) coming from the north-west: syria, egypt, north africa qarn al-manazil (as-sayl al-kabir) coming from najd and the east yalamlam (as-sa‘diyyah) coming from yemen and the south dhat ‘irq coming from iraq already in makkah? just go outside the haram boundary, e.g. masjid ‘a’ishah at tan‘im, and enter ihram there. sahih al-bukhari 1524, sahih muslim 1181; dhat ‘irq: sahih al-bukhari 1531 flying from pakistan? your flight crosses the meeqat before jeddah, so be in ihram before then. how to do it on the plane what do i do now? 1 get clean. first, trim your nails, remove unwanted hair and take a full bath (ghusl). men may put perfume on the body, not the clothes, before the intention. sunnah 2 now, put on your ihram clothes. see “men” and “women” below. must 3 pray, if it is a prayer time. it is good to enter ihram after a prayer. scholars differ many scholars recommend 2 rak‘ahs for ihram; others say there is no special ihram prayer. 4 at or before the meeqat, make your intention. intend umrah in your heart and say: “labbayka ‘umratan.” must 5 now, say the talbiyah often. men say it aloud, women quietly. keep saying it until you begin tawaf. sunnah men two white, unstitched sheets: one round the waist, one over the shoulders. head uncovered. open sandals. women your normal loose, modest clothes, any colour. no niqab and no gloves. more for women bath before ihram: jami‘ at-tirmidhi 830 · perfume before ihram: sahih al-bukhari 1539 · wording of the intention: sahih muslim 1251 · raising the voice in the talbiyah: sunan abi dawud 1814 what do i say? 1 · intention at the meeqat لَبَّيْكَ عُمْرَةً labbayka ‘umratan meaning: here i am, o allah, for umrah. based on the prophet’s ﷺ wording “labbayka ‘umratan wa ḥajjan” for umrah with hajj · sahih muslim 1251 2 · talbiyah, again and again لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ labbayka-llāhumma labbayk. labbayka lā sharīka laka labbayk. inna-l-ḥamda wa-n-ni‘mata laka wa-l-mulk. lā sharīka lak. meaning: here i am, o allah, here i am. here i am, you have no partner, here i am. all praise and blessings are yours, and all dominion. you have no partner. sahih al-bukhari 1549 · sahih muslim 1184 optional · if you fear you may not finish (illness, age) اللَّهُمَّ مَحِلِّي حَيْثُ حَبَسْتَنِي allāhumma maḥillī ḥaythu ḥabastanī meaning: o allah, i will leave ihram wherever you stop me. sahih al-bukhari 5089 · sahih muslim 1207 now in ihram: avoid perfume or scented soap, cream or wipes cutting or removing hair or nails marital relations and intimacy; a marriage contract hunting animals arguing, bad language, sins men: fitted, stitched clothing (shirts, trousers, underwear); covering the head women: niqab and gloves qur’an 2:197 · sahih al-bukhari 1542, 1838 allowed in ihram showering with unscented soap · changing your ihram sheets · watch, glasses, belt, money pouch · umbrella · bandages and medicine. remember flying in? most scholars say enter ihram before the plane passes the meeqat, not after landing at jeddah. some allow jeddah for certain routes. follow the scholar you trust. made a mistake in ihram? don’t panic, this happens to many people. things done by forgetting or not knowing are treated gently; some mistakes need a compensation (fidyah). just ask a scholar. forgetting or not knowing: qur’an 2:286 · compensation (fidyah): qur’an 2:196 · meeqat for air travel: see scholarly notes back next · step 3 enter makkah

title: Step 3 · Entering Makkah
text: step 3 of 8 entering makkah 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 03 entering makkah مكة you are in ihram now. keep saying the talbiyah, settle in, and let’s get ready for the masjid together. where am i? on the way to makkah / at your hotel what do i do now? 1 keep saying the talbiyah on the way. sunnah 2 check in and rest if you need to. there’s no rush. it is fine to sleep or eat before tawaf. when you are rested, you make fewer mistakes. optional 3 take a bath if easy, then make wudu. the prophet ﷺ bathed before entering makkah. wudu is needed for tawaf. wudu: must for tawaf 4 agree a meeting point with your group, in case you get separated. pick a masjid gate by its number and name, and write it in my info so you don’t forget. practical 5 take only what you need, and keep it light. water, phone, charger, a bag for your shoes, this guide. talbiyah until the haram, and bathing before makkah: sahih al-bukhari 1573 · wudu before tawaf: sahih al-bukhari 1614 what do i say? talbiyah, until you begin tawaf لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ labbayka-llāhumma labbayk. labbayka lā sharīka laka labbayk. inna-l-ḥamda wa-n-ni‘mata laka wa-l-mulk. lā sharīka lak. meaning: here i am, o allah, here i am. here i am, you have no partner, here i am. all praise and blessings are yours, and all dominion. you have no partner. sahih al-bukhari 1549 · sahih muslim 1184 arriving at your hotel (a new place) أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ a‘ūdhu bi-kalimāti-llāhi-t-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq. meaning: i seek refuge in the perfect words of allah from the evil of what he has created. sahih muslim 2708 you can also remember allah in your own words, in any language. he hears you. remember patience is part of your umrah there will be crowds, heat and long walks. be gentle with others, and with yourself too. avoid leaving the hotel without knowing how to get back. take a quick photo of the hotel name and street before you go. bath before entering makkah: sahih al-bukhari 1573 back next · step 4 enter the masjid

title: Step 4 · Entering Masjid al-Haram
text: step 4 of 8 entering the masjid 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 04 entering masjid al-haram this is the great mosque around the ka‘bah. enter calmly, and let’s walk to the tawaf area (the mataf ). where am i? at a gate of masjid al-haram what do i do now? 1 first, note your gate. take a photo of the gate number and name, so you can find your way back. put your shoes in your bag. practical 2 step in with your right foot and say the entry dua. sunnah 3 walk calmly to the mataf. very crowded? don’t worry, tawaf on the upper floors is valid too. it is longer, but calmer. your choice 4 when you see the ka‘bah, pause and make dua. ask allah for anything, in your own language. there is no fixed dua you must say here, so speak from your heart. 5 if the prayer is starting, join it first. then, when you are ready, begin tawaf. starting with the right: sahih al-bukhari 168 · entry dua: sahih muslim 713 what do i say? entering (right foot first) بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ، اللَّهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ bismillāh, wa-ṣ-ṣalātu wa-s-salāmu ‘alā rasūlillāh. allāhumma-ftaḥ lī abwāba raḥmatik. meaning: in the name of allah, and peace and blessings on the messenger of allah. o allah, open for me the doors of your mercy. sahih muslim 713 · sunan abi dawud 465 leaving the masjid, left foot first اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ allāhumma innī as’aluka min faḍlik. meaning: o allah, i ask you from your bounty. sahih muslim 713 remember if you get lost stay calm. go to the nearest gate, read its number, and call your group. masjid staff are there to help. open my info avoid stopping in walkways for photos. letting children walk ahead without a meeting plan. women on their period wait before entering for tawaf. don’t worry, there is a way. read what to do women on their period: sahih al-bukhari 305 back next · step 5 begin tawaf

title: Step 5 · Tawaf
text: step 5 of 8 tawaf 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 05 · essential tawaf الطواف now, let’s walk around the ka‘bah 7 times , keeping it on your left . we start and end at the black stone. where am i? in the mataf, around the ka‘bah anticlockwise. keep the ka‘bah on your left all the time. to find your start, look for the green light on the masjid wall in line with the black stone. what do i do now? before you start make sure you have wudu. you can stop saying the talbiyah now. men: uncover your right shoulder (sheet under the right arm, over the left shoulder), only for this tawaf. 1 stand in line with the black stone. in your heart, intend tawaf. must 2 touch or kiss the black stone, but only if it is easy. usually it isn’t, and that’s okay. just face it, raise your right hand toward it and say “allāhu akbar”. sunnah 3 now start walking, with the ka‘bah on your left. stay outside the low curved wall (hijr isma‘il) as you go round. it is part of the ka‘bah. must 4 men: in rounds 1 to 3, walk a little briskly if you can. take short, quick steps (ramal). walk at a normal pace in rounds 4 to 7. in heavy crowds, just leave it. sunnah 5 at the yemeni corner, touch it with your right hand if it is easy. if you can’t, just keep walking. no need to point. sunnah 6 each time you pass the black stone line, that’s one round done. raise your right hand and say “allāhu akbar”. then tap the counter below so we keep count together. 7 after round 7, your tawaf is complete. alhamdulillah. men: now cover your right shoulder again. uncovering the right shoulder: sunan abi dawud 1883 · brisk walk: sahih muslim 1218 · hijr isma‘il is part of the ka‘bah: sahih muslim 1333 · touching the yemeni corner: sahih al-bukhari 1609 · takbir at the black stone: sahih al-bukhari 1613 round counter you are on round 1 of 7 alhamdulillah 7 rounds done 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 i passed the black stone +1 undo lost count? don’t worry. go with the lower number you are sure of. what do i say? at the black stone, every round اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ allāhu akbar meaning: allah is the greatest. sahih al-bukhari 1613. many also say “bismillāh” first, reported from ibn ‘umar. between the yemeni corner and the black stone رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ rabbanā ātinā fi-d-dunyā ḥasanah, wa fi-l-ākhirati ḥasanah, wa qinā ‘adhāba-n-nār. meaning: our lord, give us good in this world and good in the hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the fire. qur’an 2:201 · sunan abi dawud 1892 suggested during tawaf: the dua of ibrahim and isma‘il رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ rabbanā taqabbal minnā, innaka anta-s-samī‘u-l-‘alīm. meaning: our lord, accept this from us. you are the all-hearing, the all-knowing. qur’an 2:127 · a suggestion, not required the rest of the time: your own words there is no fixed dua for each round. make dua in any language you like, remember allah, or recite qur’an. more suggested duas remember prayer called during tawaf? join the prayer right where you are. afterwards, carry on from that same point. wudu broke during tawaf? don’t worry. step out, renew your wudu and come back. scholars differ on whether you continue or restart, so ask your scholar. tired or in a wheelchair? that’s fine. tawaf in a wheelchair, or on the upper floors, is valid. see care guidance with a baby or child? if you carry your child, one tawaf can count for both of you if you intend it (scholars differ). prams are not allowed on the ground floor around the ka‘bah. families guide tawaf while riding: sahih al-bukhari 1607, 1619 avoid these mistakes walking inside hijr isma‘il. that round won’t count, so stay outside the wall. pushing to reach the black stone. hurting others is a sin; touching it is only sunnah. please be gentle. touching the ka‘bah cloth in ihram. it is perfumed, so keep your hands back. loud group duas and stopping in the flow for photos. let’s keep it calm for everyone. hijr isma‘il: sahih muslim 1333 back next · step 6 after tawaf

title: Step 6 · After Tawaf
text: step 6 of 8 after tawaf 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 06 after tawaf now pray two short rak‘ahs, drink zamzam, and then we head to safa for sa‘i. where am i? near maqam ibrahim, or anywhere in the masjid what do i do now? 1 men: now cover both shoulders. 2 pray 2 rak‘ahs behind maqam ibrahim, if you find space. if it’s crowded, pray anywhere in the masjid, that’s fine. just don’t pray in the path of people doing tawaf. recite surah al-kafirun and surah al-ikhlas, one in each rak‘ah (sahih muslim 1218). strongly recommended some scholars consider these 2 rak‘ahs required. 3 now drink zamzam water and make dua. you’ll find coolers of zamzam all around the masjid. sunnah 4 if it is easy, touch the black stone once more. only if it is not crowded. otherwise, just skip it. sunnah, if easy 5 follow the signs to the mas‘a (safa and marwah). let’s go. it’s fine to rest a little first. take your time. what do i say? walking to maqam ibrahim (optional) وَاتَّخِذُوا مِنْ مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مُصَلًّى wattakhidhū min maqāmi ibrāhīma muṣallā. meaning: and take the standing place of ibrahim as a place of prayer. qur’an 2:125 · recited by the prophet ﷺ here, sahih muslim 1218 drinking zamzam ask allah for whatever you need, in your own words. “zamzam water is for whatever it is drunk for.” sunan ibn majah 3062 remember praying at sunrise, noon or sunset? some scholars say wait until these times pass; others allow these 2 rak‘ahs at any time. follow your scholar. multazam (optional) some companions made dua at the wall between the black stone and the door. do this only if it’s not crowded, and don’t touch the perfumed cloth in ihram. times when prayer is disliked: sahih muslim 831 back next · step 7 begin sa‘i at safa

title: Step 7 · Sa‘i
text: step 7 of 8 sa‘i 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 07 · essential sa‘i السعي now let’s walk between the hills of safa and marwah 7 times. start at safa, finish at marwah. it’s about 3 km in all, so go at your own pace. where am i? the mas‘a: the long hall of safa and marwah what do i do now? 1 go to safa. as you get close, recite the verse (first time only). sunnah 2 once on safa, face the ka‘bah and raise your hands. say “allāhu akbar” three times and the dhikr below, then make your own dua. do this three times. sunnah 3 now walk to marwah. that is lap 1. must: 7 laps, safa first 4 men: jog lightly between the green lights. women walk normally the whole way. sunnah 5 on marwah, face the ka‘bah and do the same as you did on safa. (not the verse.) then walk back to safa: that’s lap 2. 6 lap 7 ends at marwah. your sa‘i is complete. all steps of sa‘i: sahih muslim 1218 · safa and marwah: qur’an 2:158 lap tracker you are on lap 1 of 7 safa marwah alhamdulillah sa‘i complete you should now be at marwah. 1 s→m 2 m→s 3 s→m 4 m→s 5 s→m 6 m→s 7 s→m i reached the hill +1 undo what do i say? approaching safa, first lap only إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِنْ شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ ۝ أَبْدَأُ بِمَا بَدَأَ اللَّهُ بِهِ inna-ṣ-ṣafā wa-l-marwata min sha‘ā’iri-llāh. abda’u bimā bada’a-llāhu bih. meaning: indeed safa and marwah are among the signs of allah. i begin with what allah began with. qur’an 2:158 · sahih muslim 1218 on safa and on marwah, facing the ka‘bah اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ. لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ، أَنْجَزَ وَعْدَهُ، وَنَصَرَ عَبْدَهُ، وَهَزَمَ الْأَحْزَابَ وَحْدَهُ allāhu akbar (×3). lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdahū lā sharīka lah, lahu-l-mulku wa lahu-l-ḥamd, wa huwa ‘alā kulli shay’in qadīr. lā ilāha illa-llāhu waḥdah, anjaza wa‘dah, wa naṣara ‘abdah, wa hazama-l-aḥzāba waḥdah. meaning: allah is the greatest. none has the right to be worshipped but allah alone, without partner. his is the dominion and the praise, and he has power over all things. none has the right to be worshipped but allah alone. he fulfilled his promise, helped his servant, and alone defeated the allied forces. sahih muslim 1218 · say it 3 times, with your own dua in between between the hills (reported from the companions) رَبِّ اغْفِرْ وَارْحَمْ، إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْأَعَزُّ الْأَكْرَمُ rabbi-ghfir warḥam, innaka anta-l-a‘azzu-l-akram. meaning: my lord, forgive and have mercy. you are the most mighty, the most generous. reported from companions, not from the prophet ﷺ · musannaf ibn abi shaybah; al-bayhaqi 5/95 while walking: your own words no fixed dua is required between the hills. make dua, dhikr or recite qur’an, whatever is in your heart. ideas for dhikr remember you may rest and drink if you need to, sit down between laps. that’s okay. wudu is recommended for sa‘i, but most scholars say it is not required. wheelchair? no problem. sa‘i in a wheelchair is valid. there are wheelchair lanes and upper floors. care guidance with a baby or child? prams are allowed in the mas‘a (enter through the king fahd expansion). families guide sa‘i without wudu: most scholars, based on sahih al-bukhari 305 · riding: sahih al-bukhari 1607 avoid these mistakes starting at marwah. that first lap won’t count. always begin at safa. counting there-and-back as one lap. safa → marwah is one; marwah → safa is the next. running the whole way. the light jog is only for men, only between the green lights. sahih muslim 1218 back next · step 8 shave or cut hair

title: Step 8 · Halq or Taqsir
text: step 8 of 8 halq / taqsir 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 step 08 · essential · last step shave or shorten your hair this is the last act of umrah, and it ends your ihram. halq = shave. taqsir = shorten. where am i? after sa‘i: barbers near the marwah exits, or your hotel what do i do now? men must a shave the whole head. this is better: the prophet ﷺ made dua three times for those who shave. best b or shorten hair from all over the head. not just a few strands from one side. scholars differ on the minimum women must 1 gather your hair together. do this in private, such as at your hotel. cut it yourself, or ask a mahram or another woman. 2 cut about a fingertip’s length from the ends. roughly 2 cm. women do not shave. dua for those who shave: sahih al-bukhari 1727 · women shorten: sunan abi dawud 1984 what do i say? nothing specific is required. just thank allah in your own words. a simple word of thanks الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ al-ḥamdu lillāh meaning: all praise is for allah. remember use a new, clean blade politely ask the barber to open a fresh blade in front of you. avoid changing out of ihram clothes, or using perfume, before your hair is cut. wait until it’s done. dua for those who shave: sahih al-bukhari 1727, sahih muslim 1301 · women shorten, not shave: sunan abi dawud 1984 back finish umrah complete

title: Umrah complete
text: all 8 steps done umrah complete الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ alhamdulillah, your umrah is complete. may allah accept it from you, and from all of us. what changes now? all ihram restrictions are lifted. now you can wear your normal clothes and use perfume again. keep praying in the masjid, and do extra (voluntary) tawaf whenever you can. it needs no ihram. a greeting pilgrims share تَقَبَّلَ اللَّهُ مِنَّا وَمِنْكُمْ taqabbala-llāhu minnā wa minkum meaning: may allah accept from us and from you. farewell tawaf when leaving makkah? it is required after hajj. for umrah, scholars differ, and many recommend it. please ask your scholar. what comes next? visiting madinah (optional, not part of umrah) going to madinah? before you go, book a free rawdah (riyad al-jannah) permit in the nusuk app. you can only enter in your time slot. the haramain train takes about 2 hours from makkah to madinah. duas to keep making share this free guide with your family after you return home arriving back (added to the travel dua) آيِبُونَ، تَائِبُونَ، عَابِدُونَ، لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُونَ āyibūna, tā’ibūna, ‘ābidūna, li-rabbinā ḥāmidūn. meaning: we return, repenting, worshipping, and praising our lord. sahih muslim 1342 hold on to one good habit from this trip: praying on time, daily dhikr, or reading qur’an. let the people on your dua list know you prayed for them. it will mean a lot to them. help someone else get ready, just as you did: share this free guide. back to home

“a treasure of paradise”, sahih al-bukhari 4205 · subḥāna-llāhi wa bi-ḥamdih…: “light on the tongue, heavy in the balance”, sahih al-bukhari 6682 sending blessings on the prophet ﷺ (full) اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ، اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ allāhumma ṣalli ‘alā muḥammadin wa ‘alā āli muḥammad, kamā ṣallayta ‘alā āli ibrāhīm, innaka ḥamīdun majīd. allāhumma bārik ‘alā muḥammadin wa ‘alā āli muḥammad, kamā bārakta ‘alā āli ibrāhīm, innaka ḥamīdun majīd. meaning: o allah, send prayers on muhammad and the family of muhammad, as you sent prayers on the family of ibrahim; you are praiseworthy, glorious. o allah, bless muhammad and the family of muhammad, as you blessed the family of ibrahim; you are praiseworthy, glorious. sahih al-bukhari 3370 7 travel: leaving, journey, return leaving your home بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ، لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ bismillāh, tawakkaltu ‘ala-llāh, lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh. meaning: in the name of allah. i put my trust in allah. there is no might nor power except with allah. sunan abi dawud 5095 (sahih) setting off on the journey (full travel dua) اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ. سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ، وَإِنَّا إِلَى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَذَا الْبِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَى، وَمِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَى. اللَّهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهُ. اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ، وَالْخَلِيفَةُ فِي الْأَهْلِ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ، وَكَآبَةِ الْمَنْظَرِ، وَسُوءِ الْمُنْقَلَبِ فِي الْمَالِ وَالْأَهْلِ allāhu akbar (×3). subḥāna-lladhī sakhkhara lanā hādhā wa mā kunnā lahū muqrinīn, wa innā ilā rabbinā la-munqalibūn. allāhumma innā nas’aluka fī safarinā hādha-l-birra wa-t-taqwā, wa mina-l-‘amali mā tarḍā. allāhumma hawwin ‘alaynā safaranā hādhā wa-ṭwi ‘annā bu‘dah. allāhumma anta-ṣ-ṣāḥibu fi-s-safar, wa-l-khalīfatu fi-l-ahl. allāhumma innī a‘ūdhu bika min wa‘thā’i-s-safar, wa ka’ābati-l-manẓar, wa sū’i-l-munqalabi fi-l-māli wa-l-ahl. meaning: allah is the greatest (three times). glory be to the one who has placed this at our service; we could not have done it ourselves, and to our lord we will surely return. o allah, we ask you on this journey for goodness and piety, and for deeds that please you. o allah, make this journey easy for us and shorten its distance. o allah, you are the companion on the journey and the one who looks after the family. o allah, i seek refuge in you from the hardship of travel, from distressing sights, and from an evil return to wealth and family. sahih muslim 1342 arriving at a new place (hotel, rest stop) أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ a‘ūdhu bi-kalimāti-llāhi-t-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq. meaning: i seek refuge in the perfect words of allah from the evil of what he has created. sahih muslim 2708 returning home (add to the travel dua) آيِبُونَ، تَائِبُونَ، عَابِدُونَ، لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُونَ āyibūna, tā’ibūna, ‘ābidūna, li-rabbinā ḥāmidūn. meaning: we return, repenting, worshipping, and praising our lord. sahih muslim 1342 8 suggested for tawaf & sa‘i suggestions, not requirements these are authentic duas from the qur’an and sunnah that suit tawaf and sa‘i. none of them is fixed to a round or lap. pick any, in any order, or use your own words. the dua of ibrahim and isma‘il, building the ka‘bah رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ rabbanā taqabbal minnā, innaka anta-s-samī‘u-l-‘alīm. meaning: our lord, accept this from us. you are the all-hearing, the all-knowing. qur’an 2:127 asking forgiveness (the dua of adam and his wife) رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَا أَنْفُسَنَا وَإِنْ لَمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ rabbanā ẓalamnā anfusanā wa in lam taghfir lanā wa tarḥamnā la-nakūnanna mina-l-khāsirīn. meaning: our lord, we have wronged ourselves. if you do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will surely be among the losers. qur’an 7:23 the best way to ask forgiveness (sayyid al-istighfar) اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ، وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي، فَاغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ allāhumma anta rabbī, lā ilāha illā ant, khalaqtanī wa ana ‘abduk, wa ana ‘alā ‘ahdika wa wa‘dika mastaṭa‘t, a‘ūdhu bika min sharri mā ṣana‘t, abū’u laka bi-ni‘matika ‘alayy, wa abū’u laka bi-dhanbī, faghfir lī, fa-innahū lā yaghfiru-dh-dhunūba illā ant. meaning: o allah, you are my lord; none has the right to be worshipped but you. you created me and i am your servant. i keep your covenant and promise as best i can. i seek refuge in you from the evil i have done. i acknowledge your favour on me, and i acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but you. sahih al-bukhari 6306 asking for pardon اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّكَ عَفُوٌّ تُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ فَاعْفُ عَنِّي allāhumma innaka ‘afuwwun tuḥibbu-l-‘afwa fa‘fu ‘annī. meaning: o allah, you are the one who pardons, and you love to pardon, so pardon me. sunan ibn majah 3850 (sahih); also jami‘ at-tirmidhi 3513 for guidance and a firm heart رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا وَهَبْ لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّابُ rabbanā lā tuzigh qulūbanā ba‘da idh hadaytanā wa hab lanā min ladunka raḥmah, innaka anta-l-wahhāb. meaning: our lord, do not let our hearts turn away after you have guided us, and grant us mercy from yourself. you are the giver. qur’an 3:8 o turner of hearts يَا مُقَلِّبَ الْقُلُوبِ ثَبِّتْ قَلْبِي عَلَى دِينِكَ yā muqalliba-l-qulūb, thabbit qalbī ‘alā dīnik. meaning: o turner of hearts, keep my heart firm on your religion. jami‘ at-tirmidhi 2140 (hasan) guidance, piety, chastity and contentment اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْهُدَى وَالتُّقَى وَالْعَفَافَ وَالْغِنَى allāhumma innī as’aluka-l-hudā wa-t-tuqā wa-l-‘afāfa wa-l-ghinā. meaning: o allah, i ask you for guidance, piety, chastity, and freedom from need. sahih muslim 2721 for your parents رَبِّ ارْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرًا rabbi-rḥamhumā kamā rabbayānī ṣaghīrā. meaning: my lord, have mercy on them both, as they raised me when i was small. qur’an 17:24 for your spouse and children رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَاجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا rabbanā hab lanā min azwājinā wa dhurriyyātinā qurrata a‘yunin waj‘alnā li-l-muttaqīna imāmā. meaning: our lord, give us joy in our spouses and children, and make us leaders of the god-conscious. qur’an 25:74 the dua of ibrahim for prayer and family رَبِّ اجْعَلْنِي مُقِيمَ الصَّلَاةِ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعَاءِ rabbi-j‘alnī muqīma-ṣ-ṣalāti wa min dhurriyyatī, rabbanā wa taqabbal du‘ā’. meaning: my lord, make me and my descendants steadfast in prayer. our lord, accept my dua. qur’an 14:40 praying for others when you pray for someone in their absence, an angel says: “and for you the same.” sahih muslim 2732 open my dua list

title: Women’s guidance
text: special guidance women e · women’s guidance umrah for women the steps are the same as for men, with just a few differences. let’s go through them together, step by step. 2 ihram wear your normal loose, modest clothes, in any colour you like. there is no special ihram garment for women. please don’t wear a niqab (face veil) or gloves while you are in ihram. say the talbiyah in a soft, quiet voice. covering the face near men many scholars allow you to lower a cloth from your head over your face when non-mahram men are near. follow your scholar. no niqab or gloves: sahih al-bukhari 1838. the report of women lowering a cloth (sunan abi dawud 1833) is graded weak by al-albani; scholars rely on other reports. 5 tawaf & 7 sa‘i keep both shoulders covered. uncovering the right shoulder is for men only. walk at your normal pace. for you, there is no brisk walking in tawaf and no jogging between the green lights. you don’t need to reach the black stone; pointing is enough. in crowds, the outer edges and upper floors are calmer. no brisk walking or shoulder uncovering for women: scholarly consensus reported by ibn al-mundhir (al-ijma‘) 8 cutting hair gather your hair and, in private, cut about a fingertip’s length (≈2 cm) from the ends. that’s all. women do not shave. sunan abi dawud 1984 if your period starts please don’t worry. your umrah is not lost. this happens to many women, and here is what to do. a before ihram? you can still enter ihram at the meeqat. take a bath for cleanliness, make the intention and say the talbiyah, just like everyone else. b before tawaf? stay in ihram and be patient. do everything except tawaf. when your period ends, take a full bath (ghusl), then do tawaf, sa‘i and cut your hair. c after tawaf, before sa‘i? carry on as normal. you can do sa‘i and cut your hair. d your flight leaves before it ends? scholars give different answers. if you can, speak to a scholar before you travel. “do everything a pilgrim does, except tawaf of the house, until you are clean.” sahih al-bukhari 305. ihram after childbirth bleeding: sahih muslim 1209. staying inside the masjid during a period most scholars say not to stay in the masjid; some allow it. follow your scholar. medicine to delay a period many scholars permit it if it is safe for you. please ask your doctor first. travelling travelling without a mahram saudi rules: since october 2022 the ministry of hajj and umrah no longer requires women to have a mahram for umrah. religious ruling: scholars differ. ask your scholar. back to step 5 · tawaf

title: Elderly, disabled and special circumstances
text: special guidance care & access e · special circumstances umrah is for everyone islam makes things easy. if walking, standing or crowds are hard for you, don’t worry: there is a way for you too. elderly disabilities families first-timers rest easy: all of these are valid you may do tawaf and sa‘i in a wheelchair or electric cart. the prophet ﷺ did tawaf riding, and told umm salamah, who was ill, to do tawaf riding. you may do tawaf on the upper floors or the roof. resting between tawaf and sa‘i, and sitting down between laps of sa‘i. take your time. leaving out sunnah acts you can’t manage: brisk walking, jogging, touching the black stone. sahih al-bukhari 1607, 1619 elderly pilgrims 1 add the condition when you enter ihram, just in case. “allāhumma maḥillī ḥaythu ḥabastanī.” if illness stops you, you can leave ihram without penalty. see step 2 2 rest first. then go at quieter, cooler times. late at night and early in the morning, it is usually calmer. 3 ask for a wheelchair or cart at the masjid. there is no shame in it. ask the staff at the gates where to find them today, as places and options change. 4 keep water, your medicines and a small snack with you. the condition, when entering ihram اللَّهُمَّ مَحِلِّي حَيْثُ حَبَسْتَنِي allāhumma maḥillī ḥaythu ḥabastanī meaning: o allah, i will leave ihram wherever you stop me. sahih al-bukhari 5089 · sahih muslim 1207 people with disabilities can’t walk? that’s okay. someone may push or carry you for tawaf and sa‘i. low vision or blind? go with a companion you trust. this guide works with screen readers, large text and audio. deaf or hard of hearing? every dua has its transliteration and meaning written out. agree on hand signals with your group. can’t cut your own hair? don’t worry, anyone may cut it for you. continuous bleeding or incontinence many scholars say: make wudu once the prayer time begins, and do tawaf with that wudu. please ask a scholar about your own case. being carried or riding: sahih al-bukhari 1607, 1619 · continuous bleeding: sahih al-bukhari 228 families & children a child’s umrah is valid , and you, the parent, are rewarded. for a young child, you make the intention and carry them. sahih muslim 1336 1 put an id band on every child. your phone number, hotel name and the child’s name. 2 take a photo of each child every morning. then you can show anyone what they are wearing today. 3 agree on a meeting gate and teach it to your children. “if you are lost, stay still and tell a guard: gate [number].” 4 take turns. take turns: one adult does tawaf while another rests with the small children. full guide: families, children & babies first-time pilgrims it is normal to feel overwhelmed. stop, take a breath, and open this guide. i’m right here with you. only 4 things are essential. everything else is a bonus, so don’t be hard on yourself. walk on the outer edge of the crowd. it is a little longer, but much calmer. use the round and lap counters, so you don’t have to worry about counting. if you’re ever unsure, just ask your group leader or a scholar at the masjid. back to umrah steps

title: Common mistakes and questions
text: help mistakes & questions f · common mistakes easy to avoid, once you know. let's look together. ! can affect validity etiquette / sunnah ! can affect validity · step 2 passing the meeqat without entering ihram. put on ihram before you reach it. if it has already happened, don't panic: ask a scholar straight away (going back, or a compensation). ! can affect validity · step 5 walking through hijr isma‘il (the curved wall). walk outside it, around the curve. a round through it doesn’t count, so simply repeat that round. ! can affect validity · step 7 starting sa‘i at marwah, or counting there-and-back as one lap. begin at safa. each one-way walk is one lap. you’ll finish at marwah. ! can affect validity · step 8 men cutting only a few hairs; leaving ihram before cutting. shave, or shorten from all over the head. remember: cut first, then change your clothes. sunnah · step 5 keeping the right shoulder bare all through ihram, even in prayer. bare it only during this tawaf. when you pray, cover it again. etiquette · step 5 pushing and hurting people to kiss the black stone. simply point with your right hand. kissing it is sunnah, but harming others is not allowed. etiquette thinking a special dua must be read for each round, or reading loudly from a book in a group. speak to allah softly, in your own words, from the heart. meeqat: sahih al-bukhari 1524 · hijr isma‘il: sahih muslim 1333 · sa‘i from safa: sahih muslim 1218 · hair: sahih al-bukhari 1727 · right shoulder: sunan abi dawud 1883 · black stone: sahih al-bukhari 1613 quick questions i lost count of my rounds. don’t worry, it happens to many people. go with the lower number you are sure of, and carry on. can i rest between tawaf and sa‘i? yes. do i need wudu for sa‘i? it is recommended, so try to have it. most scholars say it is not required. the prayer started during tawaf or sa‘i. join the prayer with everyone. afterwards, carry on from where you stopped. i used scented soap by mistake. just wash it off. if you forgot or didn’t know, most scholars say there is no penalty. can i shower in ihram? yes, you can, with unscented soap. if a few hairs fall out by accident, that’s not a problem. must i touch or kiss the black stone? no. pointing toward it is enough, so don’t worry. is tawaf on the upper floors valid? yes. can i do umrah on behalf of my parent? yes, you can, for a parent who has passed away or is too old or ill to travel. the prophet ﷺ told a man to “perform hajj and umrah on behalf of your father”. do your own umrah first. then, for theirs, make the intention for them at the meeqat. sunan abi dawud 1810, 1811 (sahih). scholars differ on the details can i do more than one umrah on this trip? scholars differ here. some allow it, going out to the meeqat (often masjid ‘a’ishah at tan‘im) for each one. others advise spending that time in extra tawaf and prayer instead. follow the scholar you trust. can my child wear ihram? yes, of course. a child’s umrah is valid, and you, the parent, are rewarded too. for a young child, you make the intention and gently help them through each step. sahih muslim 1336. families & children can men wear a face mask in ihram? scholars differ. many allow it when there is a need, such as illness or dense crowds; others say men should not cover the face in ihram. follow the scholar you trust. still unsure? that’s okay. ask your group leader or a scholar at the masjid. scholarly notes

title: Sources and scholarly notes
text: reference sources & notes for those who want more how this guide handles differences the main steps follow widely held positions. where the recognised schools of fiqh differ, we tell you openly with a scholars differ label and explain it here. if you follow a particular school or scholar, please follow them. review status content to be reviewed and signed off by [reviewing scholar / institution] before publication. version [x.x], [date]. scholarly notes is umrah obligatory? shafi‘i and hanbali scholars: obligatory once in a lifetime for those able. hanafi and maliki scholars: a strongly emphasised sunnah. “essential” acts schools differ on which acts are pillars (rukn) and which are obligations (wajib). we call all four “essential” simply because every pilgrim performs them. wudu for tawaf the majority hold it is a condition. hanafi scholars hold it is obligatory but not a condition. if your wudu breaks during tawaf, views differ on whether to continue or start again. ihram prayer many scholars recommend 2 rak‘ahs before ihram. others hold there is no prayer specific to ihram; you simply enter ihram after an obligatory prayer if it is time. two rak‘ahs after tawaf the majority: sunnah. hanafi scholars: wajib. views also differ on praying them at disliked times. minimum hair to cut (men) views include: the whole head, most of the head, a quarter of the head, or three hairs. shaving, or shortening from the whole head, satisfies all views, so it is the safest choice. meeqat for air travellers most scholars: put on ihram before your plane crosses the meeqat. some consider jeddah a valid place for certain arrivals. farewell tawaf after umrah obligatory after hajj. for umrah, some scholars say obligatory, others recommended. women’s face covering in ihram niqab is not worn. many allow lowering a cloth near non-mahram men; views differ on whether it may touch the face. (the report in abu dawud 1833 is graded weak by al-albani.) menstruation and the masjid most scholars: a menstruating woman does not stay in the masjid. some permit it. what we removed, and why some polysaccharide within 3 years, at least 10 days before arrival. polio and yellow fever only for listed countries. covid-19 only for 65+, pregnant women and chronic illness. permits (ministry of hajj title: Before you go · planner
text: step 1 · planner before you go countdown planner before you go a simple countdown, so nothing is left to the last minute. tick things off as you go; your ticks stay saved on this phone. 8 weeks eight weeks before first, choose your dates and how you will book: through an approved umrah agent, or directly on nusuk. check that your passport is valid for at least 6 months from your travel date. decide on your visa: an umrah visa, or a saudi visit or tourist visa. book your meningitis (acyw) vaccine now. it must be given at least 10 days before you arrive, so don't leave it late. flying from pakistan? you will also need the polio vaccine (at least 4 weeks before) and the nadra-linked vaccine card. see travelling from pakistan . elderly, pregnant, or living with a long-term condition? please talk to your doctor about the trip, the heat and the walking. start walking every day. umrah means several kilometres on foot; sa‘i alone is about 3 km. a little practice now will help a lot. 4 weeks four weeks before create your nusuk account. i'll walk you through it below. book a licensed hotel and make sure it is recorded in nusuk masar (needed for the umrah visa). book your airport transfers. going to madinah? book the haramain train through official saudi arabia railways channels. learn the 4 essential acts, and practise the talbiyah out loud. it will soon feel natural. women: please read the women’s guidance. families: read families & children. 1 week one week before pack using the list in step 1. men: keep your ihram in your hand luggage. keep your medicines in their original packs, with prescriptions, in your hand luggage. money: take some saudi riyals in cash, and a bank card that works abroad. let your bank know you are travelling. phone: set up roaming, or plan to buy a saudi sim or esim when you arrive (you will need your passport). install this guide on your phone and open every page once, so i'm with you even offline. fill in my info , then print your quick card. start my dua list : ask your family and friends what they would like you to pray for. 1 day the day you travel trim your nails, remove unwanted hair, and take a bath (ghusl). plan where you will enter ihram. flying? you must be in ihram before the plane passes the meeqat, so many men put on the ihram at home or at the airport. keep your passport, visa, nusuk permit and tickets together in one pouch, on you. as you set off, say the dua for leaving home and the travel dua (in duas & dhikr). nusuk, step by step 1 download nusuk only from your official app store. it is the official platform of the ministry of hajj and umrah. please stay away from look-alike apps and websites. 2 create your account. keep your passport and visa details handy. 3 book your umrah permit. choose your date and time. you cannot enter for umrah before your permit time, so plan around it. 4 visiting madinah? book your rawdah permit too. it is free. men and women have separate times. 5 keep your permits ready to show. take a screenshot, just in case you have no signal. health in the heat drink often , before you feel thirsty. you'll find zamzam all around the masjid. use an umbrella in the sun (allowed in ihram), and try to go at cooler times. feet: wear sandals you have already walked in. carry plasters, just in case of blisters. chafing (men in ihram): use an unscented anti-chafe cream or petroleum jelly. it really helps. diabetes: keep snacks and your glucose kit with you; long walks can lower your sugar. signs of heat exhaustion dizziness, headache, nausea, heavy sweating or confusion. stop, get into the shade, drink water, and ask for help. don't push on. in an emergency in makkah, call 911. practical tips shoes: carry them in a small bag instead of leaving them at the door. it saves you a long search later. carry light: your phone, water, this guide, a little cash and your hotel card. leave valuables at the hotel. crowds change with the season and prayer times. ask your group leader when it is usually calmer. stay charged: a power bank keeps this guide, your counters and your nusuk permits working all day. avoid unofficial visa, nusuk or train websites that ask for payment. leaving the vaccine to the last week. it must be at least 10 days before you arrive. wearing brand-new shoes on the day of umrah. checked september 2026: vaccine rules, saudi ministry of health (umrah 1447h); permits and nusuk masar, ministry of hajj and umrah. rules change each season; check again before booking. step 1 next · step 2 enter ihram

title: Visiting Madinah
text: optional · after umrah visiting madinah optional · not part of umrah visiting madinah المدينة most pilgrims also visit the prophet’s mosque in madinah. it is a separate, blessed visit, and your umrah is complete without it. where am i? madinah, at masjid an-nabawi why visit “one prayer in my mosque is better than a thousand prayers in any other mosque, except al-masjid al-haram.” sahih al-bukhari 1190 . it is one of only three mosques the prophet ﷺ encouraged travelling to. sahih al-bukhari 1189 what do i do? 1 step into the masjid with your right foot and say the entry dua. it’s the same dua as in makkah. you don’t need ihram in madinah. sunnah 2 pray two rak‘ahs to greet the masjid. just as you would in any mosque, if it is not a prayer time. sunnah 3 pray in the rawdah, with your nusuk permit. “between my house and my pulpit is a garden of the gardens of paradise.” please enter only in your booked time slot. men and women have separate times. permit needed 4 greet the prophet ﷺ, then abu bakr and ‘umar. walk calmly along the grave area, say your salam softly, and keep moving with the line. 5 visit masjid quba. first make wudu where you are staying, then go and pray there. the prophet ﷺ said this carries a reward like that of an umrah. sunnah 6 if you wish, you can also visit al-baqi‘ and the martyrs of uhud. greet those buried there with the graveyard dua below, and pray for them. optional rawdah: sahih al-bukhari 1196 · quba: sunan ibn majah 1412 (hasan) what do i say? entering the masjid, right foot first بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ، اللَّهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ bismillāh, wa-ṣ-ṣalātu wa-s-salāmu ‘alā rasūlillāh. allāhumma-ftaḥ lī abwāba raḥmatik. meaning: in the name of allah, and peace and blessings on the messenger of allah. o allah, open for me the doors of your mercy. sahih muslim 713 · sunan abi dawud 465 greeting at the grave of the prophet ﷺ السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا عُمَرُ as-salāmu ‘alayka yā rasūla-llāh. as-salāmu ‘alayka yā abā bakr. as-salāmu ‘alayka yā ‘umar. meaning: peace be upon you, o messenger of allah. peace be upon you, o abu bakr. peace be upon you, o ‘umar. the greeting of ibn ‘umar, who said “o my father” for ‘umar · al-bayhaqi, al-sunan al-kubra 10271 visiting al-baqi‘ or any graveyard السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الدِّيَارِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُسْلِمِينَ، وَإِنَّا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَلَاحِقُونَ، أَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ لَنَا وَلَكُمُ الْعَافِيَةَ as-salāmu ‘alaykum ahla-d-diyāri mina-l-mu’minīna wa-l-muslimīn, wa innā in shā’a-llāhu la-lāḥiqūn, as’alu-llāha lanā wa lakumu-l-‘āfiyah. meaning: peace be upon you, o believers and muslims who dwell here. we will, if allah wills, join you. i ask allah for well-being for us and for you. sahih muslim 975 leaving the masjid, left foot first اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ allāhumma innī as’aluka min faḍlik. meaning: o allah, i ask you from your bounty. sahih muslim 713 send blessings on the prophet ﷺ often you’ll find the full salawat in duas & dhikr. remember going from madinah to makkah for umrah? remember to enter ihram at the madinah meeqat, dhul-hulayfah (abyar ‘ali), before you continue. the haramain train takes about 2 hours. rawdah permit book it in the nusuk app before you arrive, because you cannot enter outside your slot. women visiting graveyards scholars differ on this. please follow your scholar, and check the current visiting arrangements when you are there. dhul-hulayfah: sahih al-bukhari 1524 · train: saudi arabia railways · rawdah permit: nusuk app avoid raising your voice in the masjid, especially near the grave. pushing in the rawdah or at the grave. give others space; everyone has only a little time. stopping in the walkways and blocking the line. lowering the voice near the prophet ﷺ: qur’an 49:2 back keep going duas & dhikr

title: Glossary
text: reference glossary words you will hear glossary simple meanings for the words used in this guide, from a to z. black stone الحجر الأسود the stone set in one corner of the ka‘bah (al-hajar al-aswad). each round of tawaf starts and ends in line with it. step 5 dhikr ذِكْر remembering allah with short phrases, like subhanallah or alhamdulillah. dua دُعَاء a personal prayer or request to allah, in any language. fidyah فِدْيَة a compensation, such as feeding the poor or a sacrifice, for certain mistakes in ihram. ask a scholar. ghusl غُسْل a full bath that washes the whole body, for purification. halq حَلْق shaving the whole head (men). ends ihram. step 8 haram حَرَم the sacred area around makkah (and madinah). also used for masjid al-haram itself. hijr isma‘il (hatim) حِجْر إسماعيل the low, curved wall beside the ka‘bah. it is part of the ka‘bah, so tawaf goes around the outside of it. idtiba‘ اضْطِبَاع men uncovering the right shoulder during the tawaf of umrah only. ihram إحْرَام the sacred state of umrah, entered with intention and the talbiyah. also the two white sheets men wear. step 2 ka‘bah الكَعْبَة the cube-shaped house of allah in makkah, which muslims face in prayer. mahram مَحْرَم a close male relative a woman cannot marry, such as her husband, father, son or brother. maqam ibrahim مَقام إبراهيم the stone where prophet ibrahim stood, in a gold-coloured case near the ka‘bah. pray two rak‘ahs behind it after tawaf if there is space. marwah المَرْوَة the hill where sa‘i ends. mas‘a المَسْعَى the long hall between safa and marwah where sa‘i is done. masjid al-haram المسجد الحرام the great mosque in makkah that surrounds the ka‘bah. masjid an-nabawi المسجد النبوي the prophet’s mosque in madinah. visiting madinah mataf المَطاف the open area around the ka‘bah where tawaf is done. meeqat مِيقَات a boundary that pilgrims must not cross without being in ihram. multazam المُلْتَزَم the wall between the black stone and the door of the ka‘bah. niyyah نِيَّة intention, made in the heart. nusuk نُسُك the official app of the ministry of hajj and umrah for permits and bookings. before you go rak‘ah رَكْعَة one unit of prayer. ramal رَمَل men walking briskly with short steps in the first three rounds of tawaf. rawdah الرَّوْضَة the area in the prophet’s mosque between his house and his pulpit, called a garden of paradise. needs a nusuk permit. safa الصَّفَا the hill where sa‘i begins. sa‘i سَعْي walking seven times between safa and marwah. step 7 sunnah سُنَّة the practice of the prophet ﷺ. rewarded, but umrah is valid without it. talbiyah تَلْبِيَة “labbayka allahumma labbayk…”, said often from ihram until tawaf begins. taqsir تَقْصِير shortening the hair. ends ihram. step 8 tawaf طَوَاف walking seven times around the ka‘bah, anticlockwise. step 5 tawaf al-wada‘ طَوَاف الوَدَاع the farewell tawaf before leaving makkah. required after hajj; for umrah, scholars differ. umrah عُمْرَة the lesser pilgrimage: ihram, tawaf, sa‘i and cutting the hair. wudu وُضُوء the washing before prayer. needed for tawaf. yemeni corner الرُّكْن اليَمَاني the corner of the ka‘bah before the black stone (ar-rukn al-yamani). zamzam زَمْزَم the blessed well water of makkah, available all around the masjid.

title: Families, children and infants
text: special guidance families & children e · families umrah with children and babies your children are welcome in the haram. plan for rest, heat and crowds, and keep things simple. you can do this. start here babies & nappies tawaf & sa‘i prams & carriers weather & clothes if a child is lost packing list preparing kids first, decide a child’s umrah is valid , and the parent is rewarded. a woman lifted up a child and asked, “is there hajj for this one?” the prophet ﷺ said, “yes, and you will have a reward.” sahih muslim 1336 it is optional for children. children are not yet required to do acts of worship, so your baby can simply come with you without entering ihram. you do your own umrah. sunan abi dawud 4403 1 young child: you make the intention for them. dress them for ihram at the meeqat and intend that this child is entering ihram for umrah. then gently take them through each step with you. 2 older child who understands: they intend and do it themselves. help them gently with the words and the counting. 3 ihram rules apply to them as well. keep perfume away from them. boys: no fitted clothes, and keep the head uncovered. girls: their normal modest clothes. intention for a young child: shaykh ibn ‘uthaymin, as quoted by islamqa 104345 babies, nappies & ihram 1 baby not in ihram? then dress and change them just as you normally would. for little babies, this is the simplest choice. 2 baby girl in ihram: her normal clothes and nappies are fine. women and girls may wear stitched clothes in ihram. 3 baby boy in ihram: don’t worry, a nappy is allowed when needed. many scholars count a nappy like fitted clothing. it is allowed out of need, but many say you, the parent, then give a compensation (fidyah): feed six poor people, fast three days, or sacrifice a sheep. scholars differ 4 use unscented wipes and cream while in ihram. the same goes for you if you are in ihram. 5 change nappies in the washrooms, never on the masjid carpet. bag used nappies and put them in a bin outside the prayer area. 6 put on a clean nappy just before tawaf. scholars differ on how strict purity rules are for a small child. a clean nappy satisfies every view, so you can be at ease. praying while holding a baby the prophet ﷺ prayed carrying his granddaughter umamah. but don’t hold a baby with a dirty nappy in prayer; take turns with your spouse instead. sahih al-bukhari 516 nappy in ihram: islamqa 434494 (shaykh ibn ‘uthaymin); child in ihram: islamweb fatwa 210904 · carrying a baby in tawaf and prayer: seekersguidance (hanafi) tawaf & sa‘i with children 1 carrying your child? one tawaf can count for both of you. if you intend it for yourself and your child, many scholars say it is enough. others say do them separately. follow your scholar. scholars differ 2 try to go at quieter, cooler times. late at night or after fajr is usually calmer. try to avoid friday and the hours around prayer. 3 walk on the outer edge or the upper floors. it is longer, but you’ll have room to stop, feed and comfort your child. 4 older children: help them make wudu, then hold hands the whole way. let them hold the counter on your phone, so they feel part of it. 5 stop and rest whenever you need to. there’s no rush. resting between rounds and laps is allowed. carrying a child in tawaf: shaykh ibn baz, as quoted by islamqa 104345 prams, carriers & carts no prams on the ground floor of the mataf (around the ka‘bah). prams are allowed on the upper floors of the mataf and in the mas‘a (safa and marwah), entering through the king fahd expansion. when it is very crowded, staff may not let prams into the masjid at all . so bring a carrier as a back-up. a baby carrier or sling is easiest in crowds. men may wear one in ihram too; it does not count as clothing. bring a light, fold-up pram . wheelchairs and electric carts are kept for the elderly and people who cannot walk. care & access pram rule: general authority for the care of the two holy mosques, reported by saudi gazette, 29 jan 2024 · sling in ihram: islamqa 60186 · checked sept 2026; rules can change, so ask staff at the gate. weather & what to wear months makkah (day / night) what to pack dec–feb mild 31–33°c / 19–21°c madinah nights 12–14°c light clothes by day; a warm layer, socks and a blanket for madinah nights. mar–apr warm 35–39°c / 22–25°c light cotton; cap or umbrella; one layer for air-conditioning. may–sep very hot 42–44°c / 28–30°c loose, light-coloured cotton; plenty of water; stay inside at midday. oct–nov hot 36–40°c / 23–27°c light cotton; cap or umbrella; a thin layer for the evening. inside the masjid is air-conditioned and can feel cold. keep a light layer or blanket handy for your baby. boys in ihram keep their heads uncovered. keep them shaded with an umbrella instead of a cap. anyone in ihram needs unscented sunscreen and cream. give water often , even if they don’t ask for it. babies: feed them more often in the heat. heat warning signs in a child very sleepy or floppy, hot dry skin, vomiting, or far fewer wet nappies. move them to shade or air-conditioning straight away, cool them with a wet cloth, give water, and call 911 if they don’t get better quickly. temperatures: average highs and lows 1991–2020 (noaa, jeddah regional climate center; wmo), rounded. if a child gets lost 1 before you go in: put an id band on every child. your phone number, hotel and the child’s name. wristband printing machines stand at king abdulaziz gate, king fahd gate and the ajyad bridge entrance. 2 take a photo of each child every morning. if needed, it shows what they are wearing today. 3 teach them one simple rule: stand still and show your band to a guard. agree a meeting gate too. save it in my info 4 if it happens, stay calm and tell the nearest masjid staff or security at once. give them the photo and the band details. emergency: 911 . ramadan: children’s nursery centres during ramadan, the two holy mosques run supervised nursery centres. you can register online or at the reception desk; each child gets a band matched to the parent’s. wristband devices: saudi press agency, 21 mar 2024 · nursery centres: saudi press agency, 8 mar 2026 papers for children passport and visa for each child , even babies. meningitis vaccine for children aged 1 year and over , like adults. keep routine childhood vaccines up to date. add each child to your nusuk account as a companion. permit rules for young children can change each season; check in the app when you book. children’s medicines and a fever reducer your doctor is happy with. vaccines: saudi ministry of health, umrah health requirements · checked sept 2026 packing list for little ones tick each item as you pack. your ticks are saved on this phone. baby carrier or sling light, fold-up pram nappies for two days more than you think unscented wipes, nappy cream and nappy bags spare clothes in a zip bag light blanket or shawl for the air-conditioning water bottle, snacks and oral rehydration sachets cap (if not in ihram) or small umbrella id wristband for each child a small quiet toy or book preparing your children show them pictures of the ka‘bah and explain simply: “we walk around allah’s house seven times.” teach a few words: labbayk, allāhu akbar, subḥānallāh. let them make their own dua , and help them keep a small list of what they want to ask for. be gentle with yourself and with them. crying and restlessness are normal, so don’t feel embarrassed. the prophet ﷺ shortened his prayer when he heard a baby cry. sahih al-bukhari 707 protection for your children (the prophet ﷺ said it for al-hasan and al-husayn) أُعِيذُكُمَا بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ، وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لَامَّةٍ u‘īdhukumā bi-kalimāti-llāhi-t-tāmmah, min kulli shayṭānin wa hāmmah, wa min kulli ‘aynin lāmmah meaning: i seek protection for you both in the perfect words of allah, from every devil and harmful creature, and from every evil eye. sahih al-bukhari 3371 · for one child say “u‘īdhuka” (boy) or “u‘īdhuki” (girl) back to umrah steps

title: Travelling from Pakistan
text: before you fly from pakistan pakistan · checked sept 2026 travelling from pakistan flying from pakistan? here is what you need: vaccines, ihram on the flight, help in saudi arabia, and money and phone tips. vaccines ihram on the flight help in saudi money & phone vaccines and your certificate no certificate, no boarding pass airlines flying from pakistan will not let you board for saudi arabia without the right vaccination proof. please sort this out early. polio vaccine at least 4 weeks before you fly, and no older than 6 months. the certificate must carry a government or private hospital stamp. everyone travelling from pakistan needs it, on any visa, so you do too. meningitis vaccine (acyw) for everyone aged 1 year and over, at least 10 days before you arrive. nadra-linked digital vaccine card. since 14 september 2026, border health services pakistan requires umrah travellers to carry a digital vaccine card linked to nadra, from an authorised vaccination centre. it started at karachi airport; other airports are expected to follow. where to get it: the federal government civil dispensary is named as the authorised centre, and there are last-minute vaccination counters at the airport. you pay the fees through nadra e-sahulat. a week before you fly, please confirm the latest rules with your travel agent or airline. these rules are new and still changing. polio rule: saudi general authority of civil aviation circular, reported by dawn, 14 feb 2025 · meningitis: saudi ministry of health, umrah health requirements · nadra certificate: border health services notice of 7 sept 2026, reported by dawn, 12 sept 2026, and daily pakistan, 14 sept 2026 ihram on the flight 1 your flight to jeddah crosses the meeqat while you are still in the air. so you must be in ihram before that point, not after landing. must 2 men: put on your ihram sheets at home or at the airport. trust me, it is much easier than changing in a small aircraft toilet. wearing the clothes early is fine; ihram begins with the intention. 3 when the crew announces the meeqat, make your intention and begin the talbiyah. not sure? just ask the crew when the plane will pass the meeqat. 4 flying to madinah first? then no ihram on this flight. you will enter ihram at dhul-hulayfah (abyar ‘ali) when you leave madinah for makkah. jeddah as a meeqat? most scholars say you must be in ihram before the plane passes the meeqat. some allow jeddah for certain routes. follow the scholar you trust. step 2 meeqat for pilgrims from pakistan flying to jeddah: islamweb fatwa 268105 · dhul-hulayfah: sahih al-bukhari 1524 help in saudi arabia emergency in the makkah region (police, ambulance, fire) 911 consulate general of pakistan, jeddah +966 12 668 9149 community welfare: +966 12 261 0574 sunday to thursday, 8 am to 4 pm · parepjeddah.org lost your passport? 1 don't panic. tell your group leader or agent, and keep proof of the loss. for example, a police report. 2 then go to the consulate in jeddah for an emergency travel document. etd section, room 13, ground floor. no appointment needed. sunday to thursday, 9 am to 4 pm. 3 take: the application form, 2 recent photos (white or blue background), a copy of your lost passport, a copy of your cnic, and proof of the loss. before you leave home save photos of your passport, visa, cnic and vaccine card on your phone, and email them to yourself too. consulate contacts and emergency travel document: consulate general of pakistan, jeddah (parepjeddah.org), checked sept 2026 · 911: saudi press agency, june 2026 money & phone cash limit leaving pakistan: the state bank of pakistan set usd 5,000 per visit and usd 30,000 a year for adults, and half that for children. please check the current limit with your bank before you fly. carry some saudi riyals for small shops and taxis, plus a bank card that works abroad. let your bank know you are travelling. saudi sim or esim: bring your original passport. you can buy a sim at airport counters and operator shops, and every sim must be registered to your identity. before you fly: install nusuk and this guide, and open every page once so i can stay with you offline.
